title.narrative: UNICEF & Naturvårdsverket: Förbättrad luftkvalitet på västra Balkan
UNICEF & SwEPA: Improved air quality in the Western Balkans

description.narrative:
The programme has a joint Theory of Change (ToC) with the overall objective to "support the countries of the Western Balkans by strengthening national and local government capacities as duty bearers with respect to air quality governance and air quality data, whilst also facilitating the voices and recommendations of children and youth as rights holders, to improve air quality policy and change social norms."
The focus of UNICEF will be on two outcomes relating to Children and Youth as Agents of Change and will strengthen youth-led air pollution advocacy efforts across the region. The new proposal (Annex II) will in the amendment replace the Annex 2 (Explanatory note) in the agreement signed in August 2022.
Outcome 1: Increased education and awareness around key air quality issues is now formulated as "Education and awareness around key air quality issues improved"
For the phase 2 there are clear sub-objectives with an improved focus on systems strengthening: preschool, primary and secondary education curricula and teachers training.
The sub-objectives are: 1.1 Climate change education, with focus on air quality, mainstreamed into the education systems and 1.2. Green employability opportunities and eco-entrepreneurship skills of youth increased.
The regional aspects are better developed for the second phase. UNICEF has during the first phase established contact or cooperation with e.g. EU4Green, European Training Foundation and the WB6 Chamber Investment Forum. There is even more clarity on UNICEF's efforts to support institutional development within the partner countries.
Outcome 2: Improved mobilization and coordination of action for children and youths on air quality is formulated as "Mobilization and coordination of action for children and youth on air quality increased"
The sub-outcomes are defined as: 2.1. Youth capacities to raise awareness and mobilize public support for key air quality issues strengthened and 2.2. Youth advocacy and participation in development and implementation of air quality policies increased.
SwEPA, in close collaboration with the Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute (SMHI) will focus on four outcomes supporting national and local authorities and institutions ambitions to fulfil requirements in the EU-accession process regarding air quality and emissions data, and public access to environmental information.
Outcome 1: Increased processing capacity for emissions data
In all countries of the region, there is a lack of data at the local level for developing emissions inventories, which are a critical prerequisite for action planning to improve air quality and a requirement under the Ambient Air Quality Directive. The project will together with 1-2 municipalities in the pilot countries develop a toolkit that enables municipalities to make better use of existing data and draw on pre-set data from EEA and other sources. The work will strengthen capacities of institutions at local and central levels to work with Emissions Inventorying and will improve the basis for making effective AQ action plans in municipalities.
Outcome 2: Partner institutions have improved their guidance for local self-governments regarding air quality management.
The Ambient Air Quality Directive requires countries to develop local AQ action plans when there are exceedances to set levels of air pollution. This obligation often falls on local governments. Capacities in AQ management at the local government level in the region are overall low, often with only a few individuals working with environmental issues. Dialogue with the Network of Local Authorities of South East Europe (NALAS) and national institutions in the region suggest that current guidance in AQ management mainly consists of the distribution of legislation and regulations. SwEPA will support the national level governments to increase and improve their guidance to municipalities in order to strengthen local governments possibilities to fulfill their obligations.
Outcome 3: Increased Public Access to air quality data and information
All countries of the region are reporting AQ data to EEA on an annual basis using the Raven system. All countries have databases for storing their air quality data but only North Macedonia makes some of this data available to the public. Disseminating historical data online would allow the public, researchers, journalists and other interested parties to analyse developments and trends in AQ over a longer period and would also allow governments to show results of measures taken to improve air quality. The project will develop an open-source air quality portal that will enable MoE/EPA to improve their disseminate near real time and historical data from Raven through the institutions current websites. The project further aims to increase knowledge of the national institutions to improve accessibility of AQ information for different groups of women, men, girls and boys by discussing communication and accessibility in relation to the websites and by supporting practical capacity development.
Outcome 4: Inclusive regional dialogue on availability, acquisition and usage of Air Quality data established.
Component 4 aims to facilitate the establishment an inclusive regional dialogue on AQ Management and invites all countries of the region to participate, contribute to development in the program and to benefit from the outcomes. By including topics of gender equality and rights perspective in the agendas of the meetings, the network events are also expected to increased awareness and capacity among partner institutions, SMHI/SwEPA and on girls and boys perspectives in AQ management.

Programmet är ett samarbete mellan UNICEF och Naturvårdsverket som syftar till att ta itu med luftföroreningar i regionen genom att stärka nationella och lokala myndigheters kapacitet som ansvarsbärare när det gäller förvaltning, analys och disseminering av luftkvalitetsdata. Samtidigt ska programmet också lyfta barns och ungdomars röster som rättighetsbärare, för att förändra policy och sociala normer. Projektet faciliterar ett regionalt nätverk av experter och unga för att möjliggöra utbyte samt inkluderande arbete för bättre luftkvalitet i regionen. Programmet genomförs i Albanien, Bosnien och Hercegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, Nordmakedonien och Serbien.

The programme is a collaboration between UNICEF and the Swedish Environmental Protection Agency. The partnership aims to address air pollution in the region by strengthening the capacities of national and local governments as duty bearers with respect to air quality management, air quality data as well as public dissemination of data. It will also elevate the voices of children and youth as rights holders in order to change policy and social norms, and offer platforms for youth to innovate and advocate for green solutions and improved air quality. The project facilitates a regional network of experts and youth, enabling mutual exchange and inclusive air quality management. The programme is implemented in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia.

description.narrative:
UNICEF (results by the end of 2023)
Implementing Partners (IPs) representing a range of different CSOs have been identified and contracted in all six territories. UNICEF and IPs identified youth participants through open calls in line with UNICEF criteria (gender, equity, vulnerability, ethnic background, marginalized, pollution levels in the municipality, and balanced geographical coverage in each territory).
Summary of results under Result 1: Increased education and awareness around important air quality issues
By the end of 2023, all six UNICEF country offices have trained young people directly on air quality issues, how to organize advocacy and community actions around air quality. A total of 3,668 young people (55.5 percent girls) were trained directly by the six country offices and their local partners. Youth organized 68 events/actions in 78 municipalities across the Western Balkans and implemented 23 innovations that were supported with start-up funds for their implementation, benefiting almost 500,000 people in the Western Balkans, according to UNICEF. Sida has stressed the importance of clarifying reporting on "indirect beneficiaries", as it is not always clear how the various figures have been arrived at. In the next report, UNICEF must explain how the number of beneficiaries has been calculated.
In the formal education system, UNICEF collaborates with ministries of education and relevant education authorities on curriculum revision, teacher training and development of educational materials. Three UNICEF country offices have reviewed and developed (or drafted) 10 educational materials in 2023 in collaboration with relevant education authorities. UNICEF Albania developed a teacher's manual for grades VI-IX in primary school, UNICEF North Macedonia reviewed 10 vocational qualifications, and UNICEF Bosnia and Herzegovina developed a training course for bachelor's level in higher education. According to UNICEF, the work in the formal education system in 2023 benefits almost 160,000 children and 15,000 teachers in these three countries alone (Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina and North Macedonia). Other country offices have started to cooperate with the relevant education authorities and the results are expected in the coming years.
Summary of results under result 2: Improved mobilization and coordination of actions for children and young people on air quality
The young people who have benefited from the training under result 1 have contributed to the quality of opinion formation, mobilization and participation of young people in policy work around the environment and air quality. All six UNICEF country offices have engaged and supported youth-led advocacy with relevant authorities. UNICEF has built on existing partnerships and established new partnerships with key institutions to create spaces for young people to amplify their voices and ensure their views are heard and have an impact.
Youth advocates supported by UNICEF have used various methods of mobilization and opinion formation aimed at improving air quality in their communities and increasing cooperation with local and national authorities. Young people have raised many relevant topics in meetings, panel discussions and in letters sent to decision-makers, regarding topics such as domestic heating, transport, energy efficiency and energy production.
In the second half of 2023, five country offices decided to focus on municipal air quality plans, with requirements for the introduction of measures that take into account the special needs, exposure and vulnerability of children and young people. Influence work is supported by a child and youth sensitivity assessment (child and youth sensitivity assessment) of 14 local air quality policies that SwEPA and UNICEF did together.
One UNICEF country office has started working with the private sector to promote green jobs and internships in 2023. UNICEF Kosovo has supported 34 students to complete internships in private companies and organizations working in the field of environment and air quality. Other country offices are to start dialogue with the private sector, with the aim of increasing the employability of young people in the green economy, during the second phase (2024-2026).
According to UNICEF, Sida's support has enabled UNICEF to develop a program-based, systemic approach to climate and the environment. The climate has been given much greater space and strategic focus in the organization's work in the region, not least as important integrated parts in the work for health and education.
At the country level, UNICEF has shown good results and strong commitment, but regionally there are challenges because there is not a large enough regional budget.
SwEPA and SMHI
Outcome 1: Increased processing capacity for emissions data (in targeted institutions in North Macedonia and Montenegro)
Progress on this outcome is on the expected level. Institutions started to share data through the file sharing platform HIVE, have a raised awareness of the scope of their data after in-depth discussions, and there is active participation from experts at central and local government levels for processing emissions data, especially in North Macedonia.
Follow-up from autumn 2023: Local interest and commitment have increased.
Outcome 2: Partner institutions have improved their guidance to local self-governments regarding air quality management.
Progress on this outcome meets the expectations until now. There is a clear interest from the EPA in Montenegro and MoEPP in North Macedonia to improve guidance and to participate in developing guidance materials. A proposal regarding potential measures for a catalogue of measures was presented to both MEPA and MoEPP by SwEPA.
Follow-up from autumn 2023: The catalogue of measures is currently being adapted and further developed in accordance with the needs identified in the workshop meetings. The Child and Youth Sensitivity Analysis that SwEPA did together with UNICEF has been used to identify child and youth sensitive measures for the catalogue. The catalogue will also include gender sensitive measures.
Outcome 3: Increased Public Access to air quality data and information (in Montenegro and North Macedonia)
Progress on this outcome meets the expectations so far. Experts at central level, from Montenegro and North Macedonia as wells as some others countries, participate in the development of transparent and accessible AQ data. The preliminary AQ Data Portal has been developed by SMHI and is being adjusted after feedback from stakeholders. The subsequent implementation schedule is however to be delayed for reasons outside of SwEPAs or SMHIs control.
Follow-up from autumn 2023: The update to RAVEN means the finalised AQ Data Portal will receive a few last adaptations. The implementation will then be possible if the RAVEN upgrade is deployed by the EEA.
Outcome 4: Inclusive regional dialogue on availability, acquisition and usage of Air Quality data established.
Progress on this outcome so far is on the expected level when it comes to work with countries in the region. The network meeting was a success. Progress on this outcome with relation to the work of UNICEF and SwEPA/SMHI is very good. UNICEF has demonstrated interest in using EU requirements as the basis for activities and SwEPA and SMHI have increased integration of perspectives of children and youth in AQ management activities.
Follow-up from autumn 2023: Network meeting 2 was held in November 2023 and was focused on air quality plans, as they are currently necessary in several local self-governments in the WB region. In the future, based on the newly revised air quality directive, there will need to be even more air quality plans. A child and youth sensitivity analysis of air quality plans was conducted in autumn 2023 in order to improve the child and youth perspective in future plans.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
